newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share turnover high but index slips.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share turnover high but index slips.

text.p: Nigerian shares opened in buoyant mood on Monday as more traders returned from the New Year holidays but a big drop in brewery stocks depressed the market.
The all-share index fell to 6,988.28 from 6,999.28 on Friday despite active trading involving more than nine million shares.
Nervous trading in highly capitalised Nigerian Breweries was largely responsible for the drop, one dealer said.
"Following a lull in share movement last week one dealer today lowered the stock and people sold in panic," he added.

Nigerian Breweries fell 90 kobo on fears its shares could be heading for another slide barely two months after recovering from an earlier downturn in which it lost half its value. It finished at 18.35 naira.

Recent poor results cost Chemical and Allied Products a 20 kobo drop to 6.50 naira. Container firm Van Leer, down 10 kobo at 12.30 naira and Berger Paints, 10 kobo lower at 4.60 naira, suffered for lacklustre performances.
Ashaka Cement finished five kobo lower at 16.40 naira while Nigerian Tobacco Company fell three kobo to 3.15 naira on a supply glut, traders said.
Gains were mostly in the usually active petroleum marketing and food sectors although financial and agricultural shares fared well.

Nigerian Bottling Company, the local Coca-cola bottler, finished 20 kobo stronger at 29.20 naira. Nestle moved up by the same margin to 49.70 naira, but the biggest gainer was Union Dicon Salt, appreciating 30 kobo to 42.80 naira.
Unipetrol remained ahead of other oil marketers, adding 15 kobo to end at 58.33 naira. Total at 58.20 naira, Agip at 23.40 naira, Mobil at 50.20 naira, all gained 10 kobo.
Market makers said cautious trading would persist until the budget for the 1997 financial year is released, probably this weekend.
